transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-05
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Tom Nguyen (Meridian Head of ML), Sofia Morales (Meridian Platform Eng), Liam O'Connor (CTO)

Summary:
Quick console walkthrough focusing on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Customer is evaluating Redwood for replacing parts of their current hosted inference stack - concerned about unit costs, data residency, and how to map their three main routes (chat, summarization, embeddings) to Dedicated vs Hosted. Agreed next steps: Aisha to send pricing and Dedicated template; Diego to run a token-level projection; Tom to share traffic.

Topics:
- Console: per-route dashboards and filters
- Usage analytics: token-level, user-level, time-series
- Cost breakdown: per-route cost, cost by model variant, estimation methods
- Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs: latency, cost predictability, SLOs
- Security/compliance: KMS, SOC 2, audit logs, VPC/private deployment
- Operational questions: rollouts, canary, fallback policies, KV cache behavior

Transcript:
[00:00] Aisha: Hey everyone, thanks for joining - uh we're going to do a quick console walkthrough, focused on the usage analytics and cost breakdown bits that you asked about. Diego and I will tag-team.
[00:12] Tom: Yep thanks, appreciate it. We wanted to see how your per-route reporting looks - we have three main routes: chat for support agents, nightly summarization jobs, and embedding generation for search.
[00:22] Diego: Great, we'll start in the Console. I'll share my screen now. (screen share) - if anyone can't see ping us.
[00:35] Sofia: I can see it - looks good.
[00:40] Diego: Cool, top-left is the route selector. You can create a route per logical workload, so here I have chat-agent, summarizer-batch, embed-index. Selecting chat-agent filters all the panels to that route.
[00:55] Aisha: One note - the console will show both hosted and dedicated consumption if you have a hybrid setup; we surface a column for deployment modality.
[01:07] Liam: How granular are the time series? Can we do minute-level? Our chat spikes are pretty spiky.
[01:13] Diego: We show minute-level for the last 6 hours, 5-minute aggregations for a rolling 30 days, and daily beyond that. There's also the raw token-timeseries export if you need finer granularity for a short window.
[01:25] Tom: Okay that's useful. Show the cost breakdown for chat-agent?
[01:29] Diego: Yeah pulling the cost panel - by default we estimate cost by token*model-unit-cost and then we add infra surcharge if you're on Dedicated (that's the reserved GPU amortization + ops fee). This is an example dataset. Here you can see token volume, average tokens per request, model selection (gptx-8k-like in this demo), and the computed cost column.
[01:50] Aisha: Quick caveat - our unit costs in the Console are best-effort estimates. For committed Dedicated deals we reconcile to contract rates; for hosted customers these are accurate to billing.
[02:02] Sofia: I noticed the model name shows as 'gptx-8k-like' - is that an actual model or a placeholder?
[02:08] Diego: It's a placeholder variant name; sometimes the auto transcription in Open-source docs or the model mapping shows fuzzy names. In production we'll show the exact model & quantization profile.
[02:20] Tom: Can you break cost down by model variant? We sometimes route to a quantized 4-bit variant for cheap requests.
[02:26] Diego: Yep, use the 'Model variant' breakdown, it will show cost and latency for each. There's also a 'recommended' column where Redwood Optimize suggests switching to a smaller quantized variant if the quality delta is acceptable.
[02:38] Liam: How do recommendations surface? Is there an automated rollout?
[02:41] Aisha: They appear in the Optimize tab: quality delta estimate, cost savings %, and simulation metrics based on your route's recent prompts. You can one-click generate a canary rollout config that we can apply to Dedicated or Hosted, with automatic fallback to the previous model if error rates increase.
[02:58] Tom: Nice. Let's look at summarizer-batch - that one is cheaper but sensitive to hallucination, so we can't drop quality.
[03:05] Diego: Selecting summarizer-batch. You can see here the per-request latency distribution, token histograms, and the cost per 1k requests. For batch we also show batch-size distribution - that matters for throughput.
[03:18] Sofia: Is batching automatic or do we have to change code?
[03:21] Diego: On Redwood Hosted we can enable automatic server-side batching for requests that meet merging criteria. For Dedicated you can configure the runtime batching policy per-pool. The console surfaces actual achieved batch sizes over time.
[03:32] Tom: What's KV cache visibility look like? We do a lot of RAG with caching.
[03:36] Diego: There's a caching panel - hit rate, cache entries, prefix reuse. For private deployments we can expose more detailed metrics, like per-client cache hit breakdown, depending on your privacy posture.
[03:46] Aisha: Wanted to call out the per-route cost attribution. Some customers run multiple logical features against a single model; routes let you attribute costs to teams/products.
[03:56] Liam: Security/compliance - can we see audit logs for inference requests? We need to map requests to internal ticket IDs.
[04:03] Diego: Yes we ship audit logs to your S3/Kafka or to the Private control plane. Logs include route, model, timestamp, request id, and optional metadata you pass from the client (like ticket id). For Hosted we can redact sensitive fields at ingest if you request it.
[04:20] Tom: Regarding data residency - we need EU-only processing for some of our customers. How do you support that?
[04:25] Aisha: You can pin routes to regions. In the Console's routing policy tab you can say route X must use eu-west region and cannot fall back to other regions. For Dedicated/Private we offer region locking and on-prem options.
[04:37] Sofia: How about KMS integration? We use AWS KMS and sometimes customer-managed HSMs.
[04:42] Diego: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and HSM for keys. For Hosted we integrate with our KMS but we can do a bring-your-own-key flow for Enterprise.
[04:55] Tom: Ok good. Can you show an example of the cost-projection tool? We want to see monthly spend at our projected traffic.
[05:00] Diego: Switching to the Cost Estimator - you can load a traffic profile or paste a CSV. I'll paste a small sample matching their average tokens/request and traffic curve.
[05:12] (typing)
[05:18] Diego: The estimator runs through your routes and models, applying current unit-costs and predicted batching benefits. For example, chat-agent at 50 qps with average 1.2k tokens and a hybrid setup estimates ~$12k/month hosted, or ~$8k/month on Dedicated with a 6 month amortization on reserved GPUs.
[05:37] Aisha: Again these are ballpark until we run your real traffic - Diego will run a token-level projection with your two-week logs.
[05:44] Liam: One of our concerns is tail latency during peak hours; does the console show p95/p99 per-route?
[05:50] Diego: Yes, latency distribution per route with p50/p95/p99. There's also a heatmap for latency vs token length so you can see if long contexts trigger the tail.
[06:01] Tom: Do you model cost impact of switching quantized variants automatically in the estimator?
[06:05] Diego: Yep, we simulate model variants and show cost/latency/quality deltas. The Optimize tab uses a small eval harness to estimate quality regressions on a sample prompt set.
[06:16] Sofia: How are errors attributed? If we see higher error rates after a rollout, what's the first thing we look at?
[06:22] Diego: The error panel will show error type breakdown (time outs, model errors, infra errors). Canary rollouts include automatic monitoring of error rate and latency; if thresholds breach, we auto-roll back and send alerts.
[06:33] Aisha: A quick live demo - I'll switch to the route detail and show the 'Top prompts' feature. This helps you identify high-cost prompts and potential caching opportunities.
[06:41] (screen scroll)
[06:44] Diego: You can export top prompts and then run a rerun on Redwood Optimize to see if a different model or prompt rewrite reduces token usage.
[06:53] Tom: That export would be very helpful. Is there any PII risk in prompts export?
[06:58] Diego: We have prompt masking and redaction options. By default we 'hash' user identifiers unless you enable full-text exports under an enterprise agreement.
[07:09] Liam: Pricing question - what's the surcharge for Dedicated? You mentioned an ops fee.
[07:13] Aisha: There's a reserved capacity amortization which depends on the commit size and hardware profile (A100 vs H100 etc). Typical examples: for our finance customers a Dedicated footprint tends to reduce per-token cost by ~30-45% depending on utilization. Ops fee is a separate line item in the template we'll send.
[07:29] Tom: What's the minimum term for Dedicated?
[07:31] Aisha: Usually 6-12 months for committed capacity. Shorter pilot windows are possible but at different pricing.
[07:39] Sofia: From an integration standpoint, what do we need to change in our code? We use a thin client now.
[07:44] Diego: If you're on Hosted, most traffic just changes endpoint and api-key; routes are configured server-side. For Dedicated or Private, we provide a router endpoint and can do sidecar or SDK integration. The client only needs to send route metadata to get per-route attribution.
[07:58] Tom: Let's talk about the model catalog. We have to comply with certain model licensing and provenance requirements.
[08:04] Diego: The Catalog tab lists model lineage, weights provenance, quantization profile, and known benchmark artifacts. We tag models with license info (Apache/MIT/custom) and show vendor notes. For regulated workloads we recommend pinned model versions with retention of audit logs.
[08:19] Liam: If we need to run on-prem for some customers, how fast is a Private deployment?
[08:23] Aisha: On-prem deployments vary; a minimal private control plane + runtime install is 2-4 weeks with standard infra and network access. Air-gapped installs take longer due to audit and packaging.
[08:34] Tom: Any gotchas on networking? We use strict egress rules.
[08:38] Diego: We'll need to negotiate connectivity for metrics and license verification; for Private you can fully cut egress for inference traffic. For Hosted we recommend a whitelist of Redwood endpoints.
[08:49] Sofia: One operational question - how do we handle model rollbacks mid-request if a model starts misbehaving?
[08:55] Diego: We rely on graceful fallback: route policy defines fallback model variants and deployment tiers. Ongoing requests finish, new requests are routed to fallback. For severe infra events we have global failover policies.
[09:07] Liam: Can the console surface per-customer tenant cost if we run multi-tenant on a single pool?
[09:12] Diego: Yes - we do token attribution based on request metadata and route tagging; cost can be broken down by tenant, team, or product.
[09:21] Tom: What's the typical onboarding timeline for a mid-sized finance customer?
[09:25] Aisha: From signed PO to production typically 6-8 weeks for Hosted+Dedi hybrid with standard integration. Private/on-prem adds additional time.
[09:34] (brief pause)
[09:36] Diego: I'll show the report export - you can schedule daily/weekly cost reports and have them sent to Slack/email with breakdowns by route/model/tenant.
[09:47] Sofia: We want a scheduled report to our FinOps channel.
[09:50] Diego: Easy to configure; I'll note that as an action.
[09:53] Tom: On the cost estimator you quoted ~$8k/month for Dedicated at that throughput - is that including support?
[09:59] Aisha: That was infra + ops amortization only; support and add-ons are separate line items. We'll include Premium Support in the template if you want it.
[10:06] Liam: Any notes on reliability SLA?
[10:09] Aisha: Dedicated customers get SLA-backed uptime and latency targets - we can share the SLA doc. Hosted customers have best-effort but many customers rely on pledge-backed policies.
[10:20] Tom: Ok great. Can we discuss the pilot shape? We want to validate cost and latency for chat and embeddings first.
[10:26] Aisha: Typical pilot: 2-4 week validation with traffic replay + small production canary. Diego will run the token-level projection and provide a canary config. We'll agree on success criteria (e.g., cost delta <= X% and p95 latency under Y ms).
[10:40] Diego: I'll also run a small benchmark on our side using a small GPU pool to reproduce tail latency under your traffic profile.
[10:46] Sofia: For the traffic logs, what format do you need?
[10:50] Diego: A CSV with timestamp, route, tokens_in, tokens_out, model_hint (optional), and request_id works. We can take a gzipped file upload to a pre-signed S3 link.
[10:59] Tom: We'll prepare that.
[11:02] (meeting moves toward close)
[11:04] Aisha: Quick recap of next steps: I'll send pricing and the Dedicated template, Diego will run the cost projection and a short benchmark, Tom will share traffic and prompt sets, and we'll schedule pilot kickoff week of May 18th.
[11:18] Liam: Sounds good. Anything else on security? We need SOC 2 and ISO docs.
[11:22] Aisha: We'll attach SOC 2 Type II, ISO and our standard security whitepaper in the follow-up.
[11:28] Sofia: Thanks everyone, that was helpful.
[11:31] Tom: Thanks, appreciate the depth.
[11:33] Aisha: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the artifacts. Bye.

End of transcript.
